test_files_changed.change: new file, 6 tests, added only -- fabric/tests/test_fabric_contract.py and fabric/tests/test_authority_expiry.py were not modified

sequence: 1. transport.pull(destination_node_id) -- retrieve pending envelopes; non-matching artifact_ids are redelivered so they are not lost
2. if no envelope matches request.artifact_id -> return CAP_FAILED (no execution possible, no capability looked up yet)
3. validate_envelope(env) -- independent hash re-verification; failure -> CAP_FAILED
4. optional artifact_index.check_and_record() -- duplicate detection; conflict -> CAP_DUPLICATE_CONFLICT

5. authority_permits(request.authority_context, request.capability_id) -- THE SOLE AUTHORITY GATE. False -> return CAP_UNAUTHORIZED immediately. This is strictly before step 6 and step 7 in source order and in every observed execution.
6. CAPABILITIES.get(request.capability_id) -- capability lookup; only reached if step 5 returned True
7. ah_interface.handoff() -- provenance/classification pipeline; only reached if step 6 found a provider
8. provider.invoke(manifest_dict, payload) -- THE ONLY LINE IN THIS FUNCTION THAT EXECUTES A CAPABILITY. Only reached after steps 5, 6, 7 all succeed.
call_path_observed.alternate_execution_paths_found: none -- provider.invoke() is called from exactly one place in process_remote_capability_request(), and that call is unreachable unless authority_permits() returned True at step 5

authority_gate_observed: fabric/interface.py, single call: `if not authority_permits(request.authority_context, request.capability_id): return _result_and_receipt(request, status=CAP_UNAUTHORIZED, ...)`. Evaluated with two positional arguments only -- evaluation_time is not supplied by this call site, so it uses authority_permits()'s default (datetime.now(timezone.utc), real wall clock).
execution_boundary_observed: provider.invoke(manifest.to_dict(), bytes(env.payload)) inside a try/except that converts any exception to CAP_FAILED. This is the only capability-execution boundary in the function; confirmed by direct invocation-count instrumentation via a spy provider (_SpyCapabilityProvider) registered under a unique, test-scoped capability_id and deregistered in tearDown to avoid contaminating fi.CAPABILITIES for any other test file.

boundary_time_result_or_limitation: LIMITATION, recorded rather than worked around: process_remote_capability_request() calls authority_permits() with only two positional arguments (context, capability_id) -- it does not expose evaluation_time for injection, and this mission's scope (test-only, zero production changes preferred and achieved) prohibits adding a clock-injection seam to production code. The exact-boundary invariant (evaluation_time == expires_at -> denied) is NOT re-proven at this end-to-end layer; it remains proven only at the authority_permits() unit level (fabric/tests/test_authority_expiry.py::TestExactBoundaryIsRejected, 2/2 passing, unchanged this mission). No unrealistic fixture (e.g. monkeypatching datetime.now globally) was introduced to force this seam, per Section 6's explicit instruction not to fabricate an unrealistic test fixture merely to satisfy this requirement.

counterevidence: None. All narrow, direct-authority, fabric-contract, and full-regression tests pass. No production code was modified and no existing test was altered to accommodate this mission.
unresolved_uncertainties: Exact-boundary (evaluation_time == expires_at) is not independently re-proven at the process_remote_capability_request() layer -- see boundary_time_result_or_limitation. This is a recorded scope limitation, not a defect: the underlying primitive is proven, and no production clock-injection seam was added to close this gap under this mission's authorization.

The spy provider proves zero invocation for a request that never reaches invoke(); it does not instrument every possible side effect a real capability provider (e.g. content_read, backed by content_readers) might have. This is intentional -- the mission asks whether authority denial prevents reaching the executor, not whether every real provider is side-effect-free, which is out of scope here.

evaluation_time defaults to real wall-clock time at the one production call site; PAST_EXPIRY/FUTURE_EXPIRY are fixed calendar dates chosen to be robust against wall-clock drift for the practical life of this test suite, not against an adversarial clock.
